raw_response:
I've been working this land for 30 years. I know what it can do. My 9 mu is split the way I always do it — 6 mu on wheat and maize together in rotation, 3 mu on cotton for the cash. Seven mouths to feed, so I can't gamble too much, but I need the cotton money for school fees and household expenses.

**Wheat (winter, 6 mu):** I'll sow Jimai or a similar improved variety the village supply co-op carries — not traditional seed, too low-yielding, but I can't afford the premium hybrid wheat. I'll plough deep before sowing, apply the usual base fertilizer, and top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I water three times: before sowing, at jointing, and at heading. Two pesticide rounds — one for aphids in spring, one for rust and powdery mildew. I've seen 450 jin per mu most years when the weather is decent.

**Maize (summer, 6 mu):** Right after wheat harvest I rotary-till and sow hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the supply station has this year. Hybrid is worth it for maize, the yield difference is real. Summer rain helps but I'll irrigate at tasseling and grain-fill if it's dry. Nitrogen is the main fertilizer — split it: some at planting, some at tasseling. Two pesticide passes for corn borer and armyworm.

**Cotton (spring-summer, 3 mu):** Cotton is trouble but it pays. I plant Bt hybrid seed — reduces the bollworm headache somewhat but I still spray often. More water than wheat or maize, more fertilizer too especially potassium. I'll plough this field. Seven or eight pesticide applications is normal — spider mites come in August if it's hot and dry, aphids early on, stink bugs later. I expect around 250 jin seed cotton per mu if nothing goes badly wrong.
